title: Binary Search

views.title: Binary Search
views.intro: One template covers everything: find the FIRST index in [lo, hi] where a monotone predicate ok(i) becomes true, with `while (lo < hi)` and `hi = mid` on true. Searching on the answer is the same loop with ok(x) = "is x feasible?".
table: lowerBound / upperBound, first and last position
Min speed / capacity / days such that feasible

files.desc: Lower/upper bound, range, rotated search and min, peak, matrices, Koko, shipping, split array, bouquets, multiplication table, two-array median, sqrt, time map, K closest

pitfalls: Compute mid as lo + (hi - lo) / 2 to avoid overflow.
Search-on-answer needs a monotone predicate: if feasible(x) does not imply feasible(x + 1) you cannot binary search.
With duplicates in a rotated array, equal ends force a linear shrink (worst case O(n)).

views.title: Binary Search: On The Answer
views.intro: The same loop with a different predicate. Write ok(x), decide whether the first true or last true is wanted, and round the midpoint the right way.
table: k-th smallest of an implicit set
Find the peak, then search each side

files.desc: K-th smallest pair distance, smallest divisor, magnetic force / aggressive cows, minimize max distance to gas station, k-th missing positive, single element in sorted array, max value at index, minimum time for trips, minimize max difference of pairs, H-index II, find right interval, max sum rectangle no larger than k, search a mountain array

pitfalls: Maximize-the-minimum searches the last true: use mid = lo + (hi - lo + 1) / 2.
Real-valued search: iterate a fixed count instead of testing hi - lo > eps.
Check the feasibility function is monotone before building on it.
